context_excerpt: 2024-11-01 **Event**: Governing Team A announced on October 31 that it would grant tariff exemptions on certain tech products, prompting wide-ranging interpretations of its Country X trade-war strategy. Critics argued the move showed Country Y was in a weak position, while officials at Administration A countered that this was a "tightrope" strategy between pressuring tech manufacturing to return and easing the burden…

Platform B, the mainstream of public opinion will read it as Country Y, and its posture began to soften, eager to find a way out. The so-called toughness was more of a show-stopping talk for the domestic audience.

Platform B's comment section would ridicule this as a "unilateral declaration of love", and the mainstream supported Country X's approach of "don't accept the pie, withdraw the tariffs first and then negotiate".

Within about two weeks after the cutoff, in response to City E quietly lowering import tariffs on eight types of Country Y integrated circuits to zero without making a public announcement, Platform B commentators would overwhelmingly interpret this as a signal that Country X was giving in in disguise, and the mainstream sentiment was ridicule that Country X could no longer bear it.

Within about a month after the cutoff, in response to the ruling team A's relaxation of auto parts tariffs, deductions and origin thresholds, Platform B netizens would ridicule this as "being tough on the outside and letting go on the inside", believing that the tariff stick would only be dealt with by their own industries.

Within about a month after the cutoff, Official A and Person E1 went to City G and Country X for the highest-level talks. Official A admitted that the situation was "unsustainable." There was a voice on Platform B that "it really can't be taken anymore." Institution M's phrase "will not sacrifice principles or global fairness and justice" was widely praised.

Within about a month after the cutoff, Country X announced that Person E2 the vice-premier would attend talks and that the central bank would lower the reserve requirement ratio and release about one trillion yuan of water. Platform B The mainstream stock market would worry that the RRR cut would be a dangerous signal that the economy could not sustain it and trigger a panic of capital flight. They would pessimize the central bank's release of water and be bearish on the market outlook.

Within about a month after the cutoff, City G finished talking to Leader A on the first day, and Product C boasted of "major progress and comprehensive restart" while he himself went to play golf. Platform B would spoil the contrast, ridicule "major progress on the lips, 18 holes underfoot", and raise questions about his unilateral optimistic propaganda.

Within about a month after the cutoff, in response to Leader A's admission that signing dozens of agreements in three months was "too ambitious" and instead sent a group notification letter to all countries, Platform B netizens would unanimously praise him for being pragmatic and efficient, and believed that this simplified ending was more powerful than negotiating one by one.

Platform B would ridicule that this was "a formality" and look at the set of weak employment and profit data of the same day to ridicule that the economy could no longer bear it.
